newsitem.title: USA: NHL-CAPS GET OATES, TOCCHET, RANFORD FROM BRUINS IN 7-MAN DEAL.
newsitem.headline: NHL-CAPS GET OATES, TOCCHET, RANFORD FROM BRUINS IN 7-MAN DEAL.

text.p: The Boston Bruins traded disgruntled centre Adam Oates, right wing Rick Tocchet and goaltender Bill Ranford to the Washington Capitals Saturday for goalie Jim Carey, centres Anson Carter and Jason Allison and a 1997 third-round draft pick.
"We are getting three high-calibre players who can lift us immediately," Washington coach Jim Schoenfeld said by telephone from the Capitals' practice rink.

"Adam Oates might be the best passer in the league and in Bill Ranford we are getting a goalie who has been world class in the past. Something had to be done just to insure the playoffs. Now we should be able to go deep into the playoffs."

The 34-year-old Oates remains one of the NHL's premier playmakers and is fourth in the league with 52 assists. He has 18 goals and 70 points in 63 games, and has led Boston in scoring in each of his five seasons there.

But he has been the subject of trade rumours since he blasted team officials for a lack of direction following an overtime loss at Colorado on February 18. Soon after, Oates was stripped of his role as an alternate captain.

"Adam Oates asked management to do something and criticised what was going on and it was inevitable after that that he be moved," Boston assistant general manager Mike O'Connell said. "We are getting three young players including perhaps the best young goalie in the league in Jim Carey."

Tocchet, one of the NHL's first power forwards, joins his fifth team and third in 13 months. Bothered by assorted ailments, the 32-year-old winger has 16 goals and 14 assists in 41 games. The Bruins also will receive a 1998 second-round draft pick if Tocchet re-signs with Washington.
Like Oates, Ranford was disenchanted with Bruins management after losing his salary arbitration case in the off-season. But he signed a new three-year, $9 million deal with the club in January.
Ranford missed 20 games with a cyst in his left shoulder, but returned to the lineup on February 15. He is 12-16-8 with a 3.49 goals-against average.
The 30-year-old Ranford backstopped the Edmonton Oilers to the Stanley Cup championship in 1990 and played for Team Canada at the inaugural World Cup of Hockey last fall.
While dealing away proven talent, Boston is getting younger players.
"We've been thinking about having to make a move to have some youth in the organisation for quite a few months," general manager Harry Sinden said.
"We see them as potentially good, solid NHL players," Sinden said of Carter and Allison.
The 22-year-old Carey led the NHL with nine shutouts last season. But he is only 17-17-3 this season with a 2.74 goals against average and has seen reduced playing time.
"Although it's only been a few years, Jim Carey's record speaks for itself. He's been a solid goaltender," said Boston coach Steve Kasper. "I expect him to do the same here.

Carter, a 22-year-old centre, has split this season between Washington and the Capitals' top minor-league affiliate in Portland, Maine. He has three goals and two assists in 18 games with the Caps, including his first career two-goal effort in a 3-3 tie with Boston on February 24.

Allison, a 21-year-old centre, has failed to live up to his potential after he was named Canadian Major Junior Player of the Year in 1994. He had 55 goals and 142 points in his final full junior season, but has only five goals and 16 assists in 52 games in his first full campaign with Washington.

Both teams are hoping this deal will spark a late-season turnaround. By rallying for a 5-5 tie with Philadelphia Saturday afternoon, the Bruins escaped the Eastern Conference cellar. But they are six points out of the final playoff berth in the East, endangering their streak of 29 consecutive post-season appearances.
Washington, with 55 points, stood two behind Hartford and Montreal for the final Eastern Conference playoff spot. The Caps are 1-4-1 in their last six games.
